title: When Wikimedian partake in civic discussion: reflections from ICF 2025
content:
One of the ultimate goals of the Wikimedia movement is to preserve and share knowledge freely, without reservation or intimidation. To further this mission, representatives from the movement are frequently invited to take part in wider advocacy gatherings. The International Civic Forum (ICF) is one such prominent platform that I had the opportunity to attend last November (2025).

Hosted by the International Civil Society Centre—a Berlin-based organisation that supports civil society sectors worldwide—the ICF is an annual global gathering where civil society leaders discuss pressing challenges, explore strategic approaches, and seek opportunities for collaboration.

The 2025 edition took place in the heart of Bangkok, Thailand, at Thammasat University’s Tha Prachan campus—a historic site central to the country’s 1973 uprising and 1976 massacre. Held alongside International Civil Society Week (the world’s largest civil society gathering, co-hosted by CIVICUS and the Asia Democracy Network), the forum focused on the theme: “Advancing Rights Together: Shaping Strategies in the Face of Aligned Opposition”.

title: Queering Wiki 2026: Wikimedia LGBT+ holds first in-person conference in Montréal
content:
From October 23–25, a hundred LGBT+ knowledge enthusiasts from over 30 different countries gathered in Montréal, Québec, Canada, for Queering Wiki 2026. Organized by Wikimedia LGBT+ and Wikimedia Canada, funded by the Wikimedia Foundation, and sponsored by Wikimedia CH and Wikimedia Deutschland, this conference marked the first in-person global gathering of LGBT+ Wikimedians and allies, following virtual Queering Wiki events held annually from 2022–2025.

The QW2026 program kicked off with a Culture Crawl, offering a guided bus tour with information about the host city’s rich LGBT+ history. Attendees then participated in three days of sessions, including keynotes, lightning talks, posters, and presentations in three tracks: Knowledge Without Borders, Queer Histories, and Queer Futures. Sessions were offered in English, Spanish, and French, with live translation and transcription available via a smartphone app.

A keynote from Constance Crompton, the director of the Humanities Data Lab at the University of Ottawa, introduced the Lesbian and Gay Liberation in Canada (LGLC) project and its intersection with Wikipedia and Wikidata in making archival information available online.

title: ESEAP Hub First Year Pilot: A Look Back and A Way Forward
content:
When BJ Sinaga started editing Tetun Wikipedia in 2015 (the Wikipedia edition for Timor-Leste’s official language), it only had around 1,000 articles and eight monthly active editors at its peak.

Faced with high internet costs despite slow speeds, the Tetun community encountered a significant barrier to access. On top of that, they faced infrastructure challenges making it hard for the community to have meetups. Aware of this gap, the ESEAP Hub took the initiative to provide support in growing the Wikimedians in Timor-Leste community. 

This is one of the reasons ESEAP Hub was established. The Hub began piloting in 2025 with a grant from the Wikimedia Foundation and assembled dedicated staff and Community Connectors (ECC) as a wider governance group. Its early focus is on concrete service delivery in capacity building, mentoring emerging communities, and community-based translation.

As the first year wrapped up, we take a look back at the ESEAP Hub’s most impactful initiatives for the communities.

title: Wikimedia Community User Group Malaysia strengthens partnerships and community engagement in Seoul
content: Wikimedia Community User Group Malaysia continued its international outreach efforts through a series of meetings and community engagement activities in Seoul, South Korea, from 22 to 25 June 2026. The engagement sessions were designed to strengthen relationships with Malaysian government agencies based in South Korea, expand collaboration with the local Wikimedia community, and introduce more Malaysians in Seoul to the Wikimedia movement. Representing Wikimedia Community User Group Malaysia were Farouk Azim (User:Ultron90) and Qhairy Zufairy (User:Qhairy), while Youngjin Ko (User:*Youngjin) from Wikimedia Korea joined the delegation during selected engagements to share the Korean community’s experiences and initiatives.

title: From one photograph’s global reach to watchlist alerts: Five small userscripts for Wikimedia contributors
content:
What can a single photograph tell us about the Wikimedia projects that use it? Five small userscripts offer a way to find out.

Imagine opening a photograph on Wikimedia Commons and discovering that it has been used nearly 10,000 times across Wikimedia projects, in more than 100 language editions. Now imagine being able to explore that information without leaving the file page.

While testing my File Impact Snapshot script on File Einstein Head.jpg, I discovered something unexpected. The test snapshot recorded 9,908 file-usage entries across 141 language editions. Persian Wikipedia accounted for 2,643 uses, while English Wikipedia accounted for 492. These figures were recorded on 2 November 2026 and may change over time. These usage entries do not necessarily mean that the image appears directly in an article’s main content. Some uses can come through templates, which is another interesting aspect of how images travel across Wikimedia projects.

I had expected English Wikipedia to be the largest user. The numbers told a different story.

title: Early Arrivals and New Connections: Road to Wiki in Gurugram
content:
From 2 to 4 October 2026, more than 60 participants, mentors, organisers and Wikimedia community members came together at Bloom Hotel, Medicity, Gurugram, for the graduation of Road to Wiki Cohort 2.

Road to Wiki is run by WikiClub Tech India and The Open Knowledge Initiatives (OKI) at IIIT Hyderabad. It helps students take their first steps into open-source development and contribute to Wikimedia’s technical ecosystem.

I’m the Community and Logistics Manager for the programme, which means I’d spent months coordinating everything through messages and calls. So this gathering meant a lot to me. I was finally going to meet people I only knew as names and profile pictures.

The first challenge showed up before the event had even properly begun. Several students and speakers arrived well before check-in time, and suddenly room allocation and swag distribution were tangled up.

title: Celebrating Wikidata’s 14th Birthday in Zanzibar
content:
Bringing people together to celebrate free knowledge, learn about Wikimedia projects and enjoy the spirit of community.

On 3rd of Oct 2026, members of the Wikimedia community in Zanzibar came together to celebrate Wikidata’s 14th birthday. It was a wonderful opportunity to learn, share experiences, meet new people and celebrate the important role that Wikidata plays in making knowledge freely accessible to everyone.

The celebration was filled with learning, interesting conversations, laughter, juice, photography and, of course, a delicious birthday cake!

We were also happy to welcome three new participants who joined the celebration and had an opportunity to learn more about the Wikimedia movement and its projects.

One of the main parts of our celebration was a discussion about the history and development of Wikipedia and Wikidata.

We talked about how Wikipedia started as a free online encyclopedia where people from different parts of the world could contribute knowledge and make information accessible to everyone.

We also explored the story behind Wikidata, why it was created and how it supports Wikipedia and other knowledge platforms through structured and linked data.
snippet: Bringing people together to celebrate free knowledge, learn about Wikimedia projects and enjoy the spirit of community.
creator: Husseyn Issa

title: WikiCamp Morocco 2026: Developing Skills, Sharing Experiences, and Building New Initiatives
content:
On October 18, 2026, the fourth edition of WikiCamp Morocco began in Marrakech, bringing together Wikimedia contributors and volunteers from different regions of Morocco under the theme “From Contribution to Initiative: Building Our Organizational Team Together.”

The first day focused on knowledge sharing, technical and organizational skill development, and community collaboration through presentations and workshops covering Wikimedia projects, open education, linguistic heritage, and tools for organizing editorial activities.

Alongside fellow contributor Adel, I participated in a presentation titled “Moroccan Darija: Documenting Our Words Before They Disappear.” The session highlighted the importance of documenting local vocabulary and expressions through Moroccan Arabic Wikipedia and its role in preserving Morocco’s linguistic heritage.

My contribution focused on the importance of recording words used across different Moroccan regions, particularly those gradually disappearing from everyday communication. I also discussed how Wikimedia projects can support linguistic documentation and the development of encyclopedic content reflecting Morocco’s cultural and linguistic diversity.

title: WikiGap Workshop at Ibn Khaldoun High School in Bouznika
content:
On the occasion of International Women’s Day, Ibn Khaldoun High School in Bouznika hosted an educational workshop focusing on access to information, information verification, and an introduction to Wikipedia and Wikimedia projects.

The workshop was organized as part of the WikiGap initiative, which aims to promote the presence and representation of women and girls in the digital space and encourage their participation in the creation and sharing of free knowledge.

The workshop aimed to introduce participating students to the importance of accessing reliable information and developing critical thinking skills when using digital resources.

Its main objectives were to:

  • Introduce students to Wikipedia and its role as a free online encyclopedia.
  • Present the different Wikimedia projects and their contribution to free knowledge.
  • Explain how to search for information on Wikipedia.
  • Raise awareness about the importance of verifying information and evaluating sources.
  • Encourage girls to participate in the production and sharing of free knowledge.
  • Promote women’s and girls’ visibility and participation in the digital environment.

title: Wikimedia Enterprise Financial Report: Fiscal Year 2025-2026
content:
This is the fifth annual financial report for Wikimedia Enterprise – for the fiscal year (FY) 2025-26.1 This report is published alongside the Wikimedia Foundation’s FY 2025-2026 audit report, as well as key takeaways from the Foundation’s audit report, which outline the full picture of the Foundation’s revenue and expenses. 

The previous reporting period was the first year of profitability for Wikimedia Enterprise; this report shows this has continued, now with net profit of $7.4M – a 92% increase. Revenue has increased 58% and now represents 5.3% of the Wikimedia Foundation’s total. Expenses increased by 28%.

In addition to meaningfully contributing to the financial sustainability of Wikimedia through revenue, Enterprise’s long term contractual relationships have assisted in decreasing the technical and financial burden of scraping on our public infrastructure. This also improves our ability to advocate for improvements in the way Wikimedia content is reused. Within the reporting period there have been many new customer announcements and case-studies published. 

Technical developments of Wikimedia Enterprise during this reporting period are summarized at the end of this report.

title: Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0: Empowering Youths Through Open Knowledge, Leadership.
content:
The Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0, which was organised by African & Proud, which is led by the two Co founders Richard Edozie and Kolawole Oyewole the Bootcamp  unfolded through interactive learning sessions, practical Wikimedia training, conversations about volunteering and leadership, team games, and visits to creative spaces in Lagos, Nigeria.

The bootcamp brought together young people passionate about knowledge sharing, community development, and creating meaningful change across Africa. For participants, it was an opportunity not only to learn new skills but also to connect with fellow Wikimedians, reflect on their contributions, and discover how their interests and experiences could help make African knowledge more visible and accessible.

From understanding Wikipedia’s editorial policies to exploring Nigerian filmmaking and contemporary art, Afroyanga Bootcamp 3.0 demonstrated that promoting open knowledge goes beyond editing articles. It also involves understanding the people, cultures, institutions, and creative industries whose stories deserve to be documented.

title: Enthusiasm Was Never the Problem: The Case of Western Armenian Wikipedia
content:
At the Wikimedia CEE Meeting in Cluj-Napoca in September, I opened my talk by asking the room a question. Who here has heard of Western Armenian? A fair number of hands went up. Who knew about it two years ago? Fewer. Five years ago? Fewer still. Ten years ago? The hands came down slowly, one by one, until there were almost none left.

Then I introduced myself properly. Western Armenian is one of the two standard forms of modern Armenian. It is the diaspora one, spoken across Lebanon, Syria, Turkey, Greece, France, Argentina, Canada, the United States and so many more. No country administers it. It is not an official language anywhere; it has no ministry and no national broadcaster, and it received its own ISO language code, hyw, only in 2018. Its Wikipedia launched in 2019. Before that, our articles lived inside Armenian Wikipedia with a tag banner. Our user group has around forty-five regular editors spread across a dozen cities, and we have never had a physical office.

That took about ninety seconds, and I had not yet made a single point.
